data.problem: India's standard meridian is 82.5 degrees East and the Prime Meridian is 0 degrees. When it is 12 noon in Greenwich, what is the Indian Standard Time?

steps.why: Simply the difference between 82.5 East and 0, since they are on the same side of the grid.

steps.ask: How much time does one degree of longitude represent?
steps.why: The Earth turns 360 degrees in 24 hours, that is 1440 minutes, and 1440 divided by 360 is 4 minutes per degree.

steps.ask: So what is the total time difference?
steps.why: 82.5 multiplied by 4 is 330 minutes, and 330 minutes is 5 hours 30 minutes.

steps.ask: Is India ahead of Greenwich or behind it?
steps.why: The Sun rises in the east, so places east of the Prime Meridian are ahead in time. East means add, west means subtract.

data.answer: 5.30 pm. India is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of Greenwich.

data.problem: A tall pea plant (TT) is crossed with a dwarf one (tt). The F1 plants are then self-pollinated. What is the ratio of tall to dwarf plants in the F2 generation?

steps.ask: What are the genotypes of the F1 plants?
steps.why: Each parent can give only one kind of gamete, T from TT and t from tt, so every F1 plant must be Tt.

steps.ask: So what do all the F1 plants look like?
steps.why: T is dominant over t, so a Tt plant is tall. The dwarf character has not vanished, only been masked.

steps.ask: Crossing Tt with Tt, what genotypes appear in the F2?
steps.why: The Punnett square of Tt × Tt gives one TT, two Tt and one tt, that is a genotypic ratio of 1:2:1.

steps.ask: What is the ratio of tall to dwarf plants?
steps.why: TT, Tt and Tt are all tall and only tt is dwarf, so three tall to one dwarf. Note the genotypic ratio is 1:2:1 but the phenotypic ratio is 3:1; questions ask for one or the other, so read carefully.

data.prompt: Work this mole calculation through, one step at a time.
data.problem: How many moles are there in 88 g of carbon dioxide, and how many molecules is that? (C = 12, O = 16)

steps.ask: First, what is the molecular mass of CO2?
steps.why: Carbon 12 plus two oxygens at 16 each, that is 12 + 32 = 44.

steps.ask: So how many moles are there in 88 g?
steps.why: Moles equal mass divided by molar mass, so 88 ÷ 44 = 2. Dividing the wrong way round is the usual slip here.

steps.ask: How many molecules is that?
steps.why: Multiply the moles by Avogadro's number: 2 × 6.022 × 10²³ = 1.204 × 10²⁴ molecules.

steps.ask: What volume would this occupy at STP?
steps.why: One mole of any gas occupies 22.4 litres at STP, so two moles occupy 44.8 litres. Note this holds for any gas, whatever its molecular mass.

data.answer: 2 moles, which is 1.204 × 10²⁴ molecules and 44.8 litres at STP.

steps.ask: Divide 867 by 255. What is the remainder?
Now repeat with 255 and 102. What is the remainder?
steps.why: 102 × 2 = 204, and 255 − 204 = 51. So 255 = 102 × 2 + 51. The rule is always: the old divisor becomes the new dividend.

steps.ask: Repeat once more with 102 and 51.
steps.why: 51 divides 102 exactly twice, so 102 = 51 × 2 + 0. A remainder of zero means we stop.

steps.ask: So what is the HCF?
steps.why: The HCF is the last divisor used before the remainder became zero, which is 51. Check: 867 = 51 × 17 and 255 = 51 × 5.

steps.ask: What is the mean?
steps.why: The total is ₹1,80,000 and there are 7 households, so the mean is about ₹25,714 — more than all but one household actually earns.

steps.ask: The values are already in order. What is the median?
steps.why: With 7 values the median is the 4th, which is ₹14,000. The huge last value does not move it at all.

steps.ask: What is the mode?
steps.why: ₹12,000 appears twice and every other value once, so it is the most frequent.

steps.ask: Which average best describes this village?

The median, because one extreme value distorts the mean
steps.why: Six of the seven households earn far less than the mean. This is exactly why incomes are usually reported as medians.
